title: Isomorphisms descend along affine-transition limits of qcqs schemes
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(B_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $B=\varprojlim_i B_i$ be its scheme limit with the specified projections [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$. Let $P_0$ and $Q_0$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with morphisms to $B_{i_0}$, and let $h_0:P_0\to Q_0$ be a morphism over $B_{i_0}$ locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For $i\ge i_0$ write $h_i:P_0\times_{B_{i_0}} B_i\to Q_0\times_{B_{i_0}} B_i$ for its base change [def-pc-fibre-product], and write $h_B$ for its base change to $B$. If $h_B$ is an isomorphism of schemes, there exists $i\ge i_0$ such that $h_i$ is an isomorphism of schemes.

source.place: Tag 081E (lemma-descend-isomorphism), with Situation 081D (situation-descent-property) written out; restriction to the directed tail at i_0.

proof.text: The isomorphism $h_B$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]; it is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] (it is a homeomorphism onto the whole target, which is closed, and $\mathcal O\to (h_B)_*\mathcal O$ is invertible, in particular surjective); and it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] (its local-ring maps are isomorphisms, so each target local ring is free of rank one over the source local ring). Also $h_0$ is locally of finite type: by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] every $x\in P_0$ has affine opens $U\ni x$ and $V\supseteq h_0(U)$ with $\mathcal O(V)\to\mathcal O(U)$ of finite presentation, so $\mathcal O(U)$ is generated by the images of finitely many variables as an $\mathcal O(V)$-algebra; this pointwise condition is equivalent to local finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion].

source.place: Tag 081E (lemma-descend-isomorphism), hypotheses; elementary consequences of isomorphism and local finite presentation

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation], [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion], and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] to the given system, with $S_i=B_i$, distinguished index $i_0$, $X_0=P_0$, $Y_0=Q_0$, and $f_0=h_0$. Their hypotheses are exactly the assumed affine transitions, scheme limit, qcqs $B_{i_0},P_0,Q_0$, and the properties in step 1. Obtain $a,b,c\ge i_0$ for which $h_a$ is flat, $h_b$ is a closed immersion, and $h_c$ is surjective, respectively.

source.place: Tag 081E proof, first sentence (only flatness is used from etaleness); Tags 04AI, 01ZP and 07RR in Situation 081D

proof.text: Choose a common upper bound $k$ of $a,b,c$ by directedness, and fix $r\in\{a,b,c\}$; write $t_{kr}:B_k\to B_r$ for the transition map, so that $t_{ri_0}t_{kr}=t_{ki_0}$. Write $Q_j=Q_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_j$ and $P_j=P_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $q_{kr}:Q_k\to Q_r$ and $p_{kr}:P_k\to P_r$ be the maps induced by $t_{kr}$ and the first projections; by the universal property of $Q_r$, $h_r p_{kr}=q_{kr}h_k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] to the column $Q_k\to Q_r\to Q_0$ over $B_k\to B_r\to B_{i_0}$: the square $Q_r,Q_0,B_r,B_{i_0}$ and the outer rectangle $Q_k,Q_0,B_k,B_{i_0}$ are cartesian by definition, hence the square $Q_k,Q_r,B_k,B_r$ is cartesian; the same argument applies to the $P$'s. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] again to the column $P_k\xrightarrow{h_k}Q_k\to B_k$ over $P_r\xrightarrow{h_r}Q_r\to B_r$, with horizontal maps $p_{kr},q_{kr},t_{kr}$: the lower square $Q_k,Q_r,B_k,B_r$ and the outer rectangle $P_k,P_r,B_k,B_r$ are cartesian, so the upper square is cartesian, i.e. $h_k$ is the base change of $h_r$ along $q_{kr}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], applied for $r=a,b,c$ respectively, $h_k$ is flat, a closed immersion, and surjective.

source.place: Tag 081E proof, choosing a sufficiently large stage and its final surjectivity argument; arbitrary-base-change permanence made explicit

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-surjective-flat-closed-immersion-isomorphism], the flat surjective closed immersion $h_k:P_k\to Q_k$ is an isomorphism. Since $k\ge a\ge i_0$, this is the requested stage.
